website_exact_old_new.old: Every case. The reviews that address this question directly reach the same conclusion: liver-directed methods — TACE, percutaneous ethanol injection, hepatic arterial infusion, radioembolisation and ablation — are less effective here than in HCC because of the cholangiocytic component's vascularity and desmoplasia, and transarterial chemoembolisation may be effective in unresectable disease particularly where the tumour is hypervascular. The one dataset that tested vascularity as a selection variable agrees: adjuvant TACE improved early recurrence-free survival only in the HCC-dominant third of 306 resected tumours (53.3% against 32.3% at two years, p=0.028) and not in balanced (p=0.276) or CCA-dominant (p=0.433) patients.

Its reduced-responsiveness discussion concerns TACE and percutaneous ethanol injection; it does not establish that every liver-directed modality is less effective than in HCC. Enhancement pattern and histological predominance are different observations, neither a validated universal selection rule. Separate adjuvant data in 306 resected tumours found improved early recurrence-free survival only in the HCC-dominant group (53.3% against 32.3% at two years, p=0.028), not in balanced (p=0.276) or CCA-dominant (p=0.433) patients.

website_exact_old_new.old: The node-negative R0 resection subgroup fared no better (87%, 53% and 18% at 1, 3 and 5 years), and the 20–21% 5-year survival after resection matches other specialist centres, so the comparator is not substandard. Three of 26 resections (12%) died within 30 days, and the discussants' point was that non-cancer deaths, not recurrence, drive much of the gap — recurrence after resection was 35% while 5-year survival was 20%. There is no intention-to-treat analysis and no accounting of organ cost: 38 grafts, 7 of them living donor, for 71 patients enrolled. The Milan jury acknowledged benefit in node-negative patients independent of resectability; that is a consensus position resting on one benchmark study and mixed retrospective comparisons, and TRANSPHIL, the randomised trial meant to settle it, failed to recruit.

Milan Recommendation 59 supports transplant consideration for selected unresectable or PSC-associated pCCA above the cystic duct, ≤3.0 cm radial diameter and without nodal or distant metastases (strong, level 3), with staging and neoadjuvant therapy specified separately. Recommendation 64 only weakly supports consideration for resectable or questionably resectable pCCA when appropriate donor access exists (level 3). These are distinct consensus recommendations, not proof that transplantation is superior for every resectable patient; TRANSPHIL failed to recruit. The consensus ≤3.0 cm boundary does not replace the separate OPTN strict <3 cm mass criterion.

website_exact_old_new.old: The Milan jury-based consensus is the most comprehensive current statement on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma, covering definition, staging, drainage, liver augmentation, the operation, systemic therapy, transplantation and outcome metrics, and it is candid that 84% of its 570 studies are observational and that most surgical recommendations sit at level of evidence 4. Its two central positions are unresolved by its own evidence: the resectability criteria it adopts are expert opinion awaiting validation while it declines to endorse any staging system for predicting resectability, and it extends transplantation to node-negative patients independent of resectability on a benchmark study and mixed retrospective comparisons after TRANSPHIL failed to recruit. Industry covered 55% of the conference's costs, no individual author conflict statement is printed, and no voting record exists for any recommendation.
website_exact_old_new.new: The Milan jury-based consensus covers staging, drainage, liver augmentation, resection, systemic therapy, transplantation and outcomes; 84% of its 570 studies are observational and most surgical recommendations sit at level of evidence 4. Hypertrophy is a specific exception: PVE is the initial technique (Recommendation 23), and upfront or additional LVD may be considered for substantial augmentation (Recommendation 24), both strong, level 3, with limited nonrandomized pCCA comparative evidence. Transplant Recommendation 59 concerns selected unresectable or PSC-associated pCCA ≤3.0 cm without nodal or distant metastases (strong, level 3); Recommendation 64 only weakly supports consideration in resectable or questionably resectable disease with appropriate donor access (level 3). Benchmark and retrospective data do not establish universal superiority over resection, and TRANSPHIL failed to recruit. The consensus size boundary is separate from OPTN’s strict <3 cm mass criterion. Resectability criteria still need validation. Industry covered 55% of the conference’s costs, no individual author conflict statement is printed, and no voting record is reported.
